head_note: code only, uncompiled (lanes never compile); T3 (FFT), D3 (denseball) skipped this round; H4 already on main as IDN_DENDRO_UNION

tsne_knn_tile_select.note: T1. IDENTICAL, NVIDIA+AMD. Block-wide mark/rank/merge top-k per 64x64 distance tile instead of the serial owner insertion; every d takes the 64x64 tile. Same (dist, idx) lists for finite/inf distances. Also the CAGRA build's exact graph.

tsne_rep_tile.note: T2. IDENTICAL, NVIDIA+AMD, needs TS_SPLIT and TS_LANE_FOLD. 256-candidate tiles, one row per thread (16 threads x 4 lanes a row), same 64-lane fold order, same Z tree. Bits none.

dbscan_eps_tile.note: D1. IDENTICAL, NVIDIA+AMD, Euclidean, not with KNN_DIRECT_DISTANCE (compiled out there). 64x64 register-tiled eps count/fill with the same three per-pair tests (landmark bound, RBC_LANES chunk-walk reach, eps_dist_sq chain); fill rows canonicalized (DEVIATION 551). Every ball-cover eps query (DBSCAN, neighbors radius).

dbscan_adj_bitmap.note: D2, needs D1 (the on arm sets both). Count pass writes word-major bit words; loop 1 keeps each range's bit-scanned CSR (kept total <= edge_cap edges); loop 2, batch 0 and the border pass copy it. Ranges capped at 25% of free memory over n/8 + 8*landmarks bytes a row (more batches at large n).

dbscan_batch_sample.note: D4. IDENTICAL, NVIDIA+AMD. First ranges = edge_cap / (2 x sampled mean degree) from 1,024 strided rows; avoids count-split-recount levels on dense graphs. n_iter_ follows the batch count.

dbscan_cc_hook.note: D5. IDENTICAL, not Apple. weak_cc fixed point by lock-free hook/compress/border, 4 launches + 1 drain per batch. Labels same; n_iter_ = 1 per batch.

hdb_mst_seed_knn.note: H2. IDENTICAL, NVIDIA+AMD, sparse arm, alpha <= 1, no trace/sabotage, not with GRAPH/KNN_DIRECT_DISTANCE. k-NN one wider; round-1 point resolved when its cheapest list weight < the list's last distance (exact cells, per-entry distance bit check).

hdb_round_one_sync_off.note: H3, default ON (waste removal). The round's ADDED readback rides on the next round's phase-A count read (cumulative ADDED): 3 -> 2 drains per Boruvka round. The off arm restores three reads.

hdb_out_memcpy_off.note: H5, default ON (waste removal). Fit outputs copied into the caller's arrays by memcpy instead of element loops. Same bytes.
